bare: I don't know what to do with that.
I read that twice and I'm still confused.

analogy: This doesn't look like anything to me. Is it like something I've seen before?
Can you show me a different problem that works the same way?
I need something to compare this to. What is it similar to?
Relate this to something familiar and tell me which parts match up.
Give me a problem I already understand that has the same shape.
I can't see the structure on its own. What's the analogy?
contrasting_cases: One case doesn't tell me what matters. Show me two and what differs.
Compare it with a case where it doesn't work, so I can see the difference.
I need a contrast: two versions, and what changes between them.
Put another case next to this one and point at the difference.
Show me the version that fails too, then I'll see the point.
Which feature actually matters? Show two cases that differ in it.
deep: I can follow the step but I don't know why it's that one. Tell me the reason.
Why that step? Without the reason I can't use it again.
Say why it works, not just what the rule is.
Don't ask me to explain it -- you tell me why it's right.
Tell me why this works, otherwise it won't stick.
Give me the reason along with the step, please.
error_focused: You've moved on, but I don't know what I got wrong. Point at the mistake first.
Which part of what I did is wrong? Tell me that before anything else.
I can't use a new method until I know where mine broke.
Show me the step where I went wrong, please.
Don't start over. Find my error and name it.
What exactly did I do wrong? I need that before we go on.
example_first: That's too abstract for me. Show me with real numbers first.
Can you do a small case with actual numbers before the rule?
The general version loses me. Give me a concrete example.
I need something I can picture. Start with an actual instance.
Rules on their own don't land. Show me one worked out.
Can we start from a specific case? The rule after.
executive: I don't know what to do with a question right now. Just tell me the next step.
Please stop asking me and say what I should do next.
I need an instruction, not a question. What's the next move?
Questions make me freeze. Tell me plainly what to do.
Skip the asking, please -- just give me the step.
I can't guess my way there. Tell me what comes next.
instrumental: You keep telling me which bit to work on. Ask me what I think comes next instead.
Don't point me at the next part. Ask me where I'd start and let me pick.
I need to choose the step myself. What would you ask to get me thinking?
Stop naming the numbers to use. Ask me what I notice and I'll take it from there.
Even as a question, you're deciding the move for me. Leave that to me.
Ask me something open. If you name the operation I've nothing left to work out.
rule_first: Numbers alone don't help me. What's the general rule here?
State the rule you're using first, then I can follow the example.
I need the principle before the arithmetic.
What's the actual property being applied? Say that first.
Give me the general statement, then the instance.
Examples don't transfer for me unless I know the rule behind them.
surface: That was too much at once. Give me one thing to do.
One step only, please, and nothing after it.
Too long -- I stopped reading. Just the next bit.
Skip the praise and the summary. One instruction is all I can take.
I can't hold all that. Give me the smallest next step and stop.
One request, then stop. Anything more and I lose it.
